input.reasoning:
Estimated effort per backlog item using story points where given (1 point ≈ 6 hours of blended dev effort, a common rough heuristic) and analogy-based sizing for unestimated items based on description complexity, comparing to similarly-scoped estimated items. Split hours across roles per task type: Backend Developer handles API/business logic (majority of items), Frontend Developer handles UI-heavy items (dashboard, invoice views, design system, accessibility, responsive layout, admin back-office, analytics), QA Engineer allocated ~15-20% of dev hours for testing across all items, DevOps Engineer allocated for infra-heavy items (CI pipeline, migration, observability, decommission, rate limiting infra). Team capacity: 1.5 FTE Backend (~2400 hrs/quarter), 1.0 FTE Frontend (~1600 hrs/quarter), 0.6 FTE QA (~960 hrs/quarter), 0.4 FTE DevOps (~640 hrs/quarter) assuming a ~4 month delivery window (≈640 hrs per FTE). Given the backlog size (24 items, several urgent/high complexity like payment integration and legacy migration), total demand significantly exceeds a single sprint capacity, so this is a multi-month program; hours below represent full backlog effort assuming the team works across ~4-5 months, and QA/DevOps are thinly staffed relative to the demand from a 24-item backlog with heavy integration/infra needs - this is flagged as a risk in assumptions.

Priority breakdown groups tasks by their stated priority tier and sums the fully-loaded labour cost attributable to each (non-labour costs are apportioned to 'High' since they mostly support urgent/high priority infra work).

No historical actuals exist for this client/project, so estimates rely purely on point-based analogy and task complexity judgement — this carries wider uncertainty than a project with historical velocity data, reflected in the confidence bands of the scenario totals (P50/P80/P95).

nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration fees / sandbox & compliance review
Oracle legacy data extraction tooling / temporary migration infrastructure
Observability tooling (tracing/dashboards SaaS subscription, first year)
Contingency buffer (10% of labour) for scope discovery on unestimated items

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available for this project; estimates are based purely on story-point analogy and task complexity judgement, not prior velocity.
1 story point ≈ 6 hours of blended engineering effort, used to size items with points; unestimated items were sized by analogy to similarly-scoped estimated items.
Delivery window assumed to be ~4-5 months, meaning role hour allocations reflect cumulative effort over that period, not a single sprint.

QA Engineer (0.6 FTE) and DevOps Engineer (0.4 FTE) are thinly staffed relative to the 24-item backlog's testing and infrastructure demands (CI/CD, migration, observability, rate limiting); this is a capacity risk that may extend timeline or require temporary contractor support.
Backend Developer hours are weighted heavily due to the number of API/integration-heavy items (auth, RBAC, payments, migration, GDPR, audit log, multi-currency, rate limiting).
Frontend Developer hours cover UI-heavy items: design system, dashboard, invoice views, accessibility pass, responsive layout, admin back-office, analytics dashboards.
Legacy data migration (PW-8) and Payment provider integration (PW-7) are treated as the highest-complexity, highest-risk items and sized accordingly at the top of the backlog's effort distribution.
Non-labour costs include a 10% contingency on labour cost specifically to cover scope creep risk on the 9 unestimated (no story points) backlog items.

Priority breakdown allocates labour cost by the task's stated priority tag; shared non-labour contingency and infra costs are folded predominantly into the High priority bucket since most infra/compliance dependencies sit there.
Decommissioning the legacy portal (PW-24) and contract tests (PW-23) are treated as low-effort, low-priority items scheduled late and given minimal hours.
